issues.description: The problem statement / UML specifies that Animal has an attribute 'name' of type String, but the solution's Animal implementation uses a private field of type StringBuilder for the name. This deviates from the declared attribute type in the specification. Although the public getter/setter still use String (so external behavior is preserved), the internal field type differs from the UML and problem text and may confuse students reading the reference solution or comparing their implementation to the model solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's Animal class use a private field of type String for the name to match the UML and problem statement (e.g., private String name;). Update the constructor, getter, and setter accordingly so the internal representation matches the specification while preserving the same public API.
